title: Comparisons and Superlatives
grammar_goal: This lesson boosts GRA and Coherence by teaching how to accurately compare data in Task 1, and weigh different arguments or options in Task 2.

core_rule.formula:
Comparative: Adjective + -er + than OR more + Adjective + than
Superlative: the + Adjective + -est OR the most + Adjective
core_rule.usage: Use comparatives to show the difference between two things. Use superlatives to show that one thing has the highest degree of a quality within a group. Advanced comparisons include 'as...as' for equality, and parallel comparisons like 'the + comparative, the + comparative' to show cause and effect.

when_to_use: Task 1: Essential for comparing data points on graphs (e.g., 'A was significantly higher than B').
Task 2: Comparing two sides of an argument (e.g., 'Living in a city is more advantageous than...').
Speaking Part 3: Discussing how things have changed over time (e.g., 'People are much busier now than they were in the past.').
when_not_to_use: Do not use 'more' with adjectives that already have an '-er' ending (e.g., 'more better', 'more taller').
Do not forget 'the' before superlative adjectives (e.g., 'He is tallest boy' is wrong).

ielts_examples.writing: The proportion of consumers who preferred online shopping was significantly higher than those who shopped in physical stores.
ielts_examples.speaking: I think the older generation is generally less concerned with technology than the younger generation.

repair_section.wrong: The weather today is more hotter than yesterday.
repair_section.correct: The weather today is hotter than yesterday.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: The temperature today is considerably higher than it was yesterday.

repair_section.wrong: She is the most smart student in the class.
repair_section.correct: She is the smartest student in the class.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: She is undoubtedly the most intellectually gifted student in the cohort.

repair_section.wrong: More you study, more you learn.
repair_section.correct: The more you study, the more you learn.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: The more time you dedicate to your studies, the more extensive your knowledge will become.

vietnamese_learner_mistakes: Forgetting 'than': Saying 'A is bigger B' instead of 'A is bigger than B'.
Misusing 'as...as': Saying 'as same as' or 'same like' instead of 'the same as' or 'as [adjective] as'.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: Living in the city is more noisy than the countryside.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: Living in the city is noisier than the countryside.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: This is the most good movie I have ever seen.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: This is the best movie I have ever seen.

image_prompt_fallback: A visual representation of three bar charts of varying heights to illustrate comparative and superlative concepts.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses an advanced comparative structure?

options.A: The more faster you drive, the more dangerous it is.
options.B: The faster you drive, the more dangerous it is.
options.C: Faster you drive, more dangerous it is.
options.D: The faster you drive, the dangerous it is.

quiz.explanation: Option B correctly uses the 'the + comparative, the + comparative' structure to show a parallel increase.
